transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sam C (Redwood AE), Priya N (Redwood SE), Luis O (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya C (PolarisBio), Omar R (PolarisBio), Elena R (PM), Ben S (Infra), Ayesha K (Security)

[00:00] Sam Carter: thanks everyone for hopping on, morning/afternoon across your zones. quick agenda — alignment on success criteria, model shortlist for the POC, benching plan, and next steps. Maya over to you for context?

[00:18] Dr. Maya Chen: yeah thanks Sam. short context — PolarisBio is building a clinical note assistant for internal R&D teams, mixed chat + long-doc extraction. must support English and French, and handle lots of domain terms like gene names, assay codes. our goals are: high entity precision (we care more about false positives than recall), sub-second interactive latency for 95th pctg on short chat flows (~200 token responses), and batch throughput for nightly extraction jobs. timeline: we'd like a 4 week pilot, moving to a production pilot in Q4 if results are good.

[01:05] Priya Nair: got it. when you say high entity precision — do you have a target metric? is it F1 or precision at X?

[01:12] Dr. Maya Chen: we prefer precision at mention-level — target 92% precision on the named-entity set for a 1k annotated eval set. if recall slips we can live with tradeoffs but not below ~70.

[01:30] Omar Rahman: for QPS baseline — our internal tooling shows about 15 interactive users during day shift with average 0.8 reqs/min per user, spikes to ~40 concurrent during rounds. batch jobs are roughly 20k docs nightly.

[01:50] Luis Ortega: okay that helps. rough math — for interactive workload we should budget for 50 rps peak, but per-token latency SLOs will depend on model selection and quantization; we can design routing to keep interactive on lower-latency variants.

[02:10] Elena Ruiz: can you explain routing/variants briefly? we heard about Redwood Dedicate — or sorry, Redwood Dedicated — and fallback models; how would that look for us?

[02:22] Priya Nair: sure. typical pattern is a low-latency model variant for interactive flows (e.g., quantized 7B or 13B that hits sub-400ms token latency), and larger higher-quality models for batch scoring. Redwood supports policy routing: latency-first for UI calls, cost/quality tradeoff for bulk. note: sometimes the auto-batching can add ~20–60ms for small requests. also we do prefix/K-V caching which helps follow-ups. (there's a slight stutter) — K-V cash in some transcriptions ha.

[03:05] Ben Strauss: on infra — for the POC we want to use your Private deployment in our VPC. security will be a gating factor; we need SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. latency to our region (eu-west) is a concern — will dedicated capacity be colocated?

[03:28] Sam Carter: yes, we can provision dedicated capacity in eu-west region or run a private deployment. for the POC we usually do a hybrid: Redwood-hosted models in region with private control plane, or private infra via our on-prem package. Sam: we'll flag latency differences in the bench.

[03:50] Ayesha Khan: on KMS — can you outline supported providers? Azure Key Vault vs AWS KMS vs HSM? also retention: can we limit logs for the POC?

[04:10] Sam Carter: supported KMS: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and we have HSM integration for enterprise. logs can be restricted; we can do minimal audit logging for the pilot while retaining necessary traces for debugging. I'll send the security one-pager.

[04:35] Priya Nair: shifting to models — we proposed an open-model shortlist. quick note: PolarisBio has a lot of jargon and some Latin species names; we should pick mixes of models that have proven biomedical pretraining or are strong generalists. my initial shortlist: 1) Mosaic-22B-Quant (13B int8 hybrid) — high quality but heavier; 2) Falcon-7B-instruct-quant — low-latency and cost-effective; 3) Llama2-13B-quant (vicuna-style fine-tune candidate); 4) Specialist-med-7B (community biomedical-tuned) — if you want something that sees more biomedical text.

[05:30] Dr. Maya Chen: curious — how different are these in named-entity precision? any ballpark?

[05:40] Priya Nair: rough expectations from prior benches: Specialist-med > Mosaic22B > Llama2-13B > Falcon7B for pure entity precision on biomedical sets, but mosaic has higher hallucination in some prompt setups and is heavier to run. the quantized variants narrow latency gaps. important to test with your exact prompts.

[06:05] Omar Rahman: about multilingual — French data is pretty formal and uses accented characters; do we need separate models or will these handle French well?

[06:18] Luis Ortega: many open models have decent French ability; Specialist-med might be English-centric. Llama2-13B often handles French okay. We should include a small subset of French prompts in the eval. If French performance is critical, we can add a francophone model (like Meta X or an LLM with better EU training) to shortlist.

[06:50] Elena Ruiz: can you propose a bench plan and the minimal dataset we should provide?

[06:58] Priya Nair: suggested bench plan: week 0 (this week): finalize rubric + dataset; week 1: run micro-bench (50 prompts + 200 doc extracts) to sanity-check integration; week 2: full bench across shortlist (1k annotated eval docs + 1k chat turns across EN/FR), measure precision/recall/hallucination rate, latency P50/P95, and cost per 1k tokens; week 3: iterate on best candidate with prompt tuning and small fine-tune if needed; deliver results + recommendation by EOW week 4. minimal dataset: 1k labelled mention-level annotations for extraction, 1k chat interactions with expected responses, plus 200 long docs for batch throughput.

[08:05] Dr. Maya Chen: 1k annotated docs is doable; we'll need help anonymizing and formatting. Omar will coordinate.

[08:20] Omar Rahman: yes, we'll remove PHI and produce a synthetic-alike set. also note we have some proprietary terminology; can Redwood ingest a short glossary for the bench?

[08:30] Priya Nair: absolutely. we support providing domain dictionaries and we can use them as few-shot context or as part of a retrieval pipeline. for the POC bench we'll run two modes: cold (no glossary) and glossary-augmented to measure lift.

[09:00] Ben Strauss: about throughput for nightly runs — 20k docs nightly, average doc length ~2k tokens. what's the cost impact for mosaic vs 13B quant?

[09:12] Luis Ortega: cost ballparks: for quantized 13B variants we estimate $X per 1k tokens (we'll put exact in spreadsheet), mosaic22B will be 2–3x cost for same tokens. The difference could be mitigated by batching and running heavier models during off-peak windows. we'll include cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly for your 20k doc job in the model spreadsheet.

[09:50] Ayesha Khan: one more compliance Q — audit logs retention, and can we turn off verbatim transcript retention?

[09:58] Sam Carter: yes, retention windows are configurable; we can disable storing user content for the pilot if needed — just need a short troubleshooting window. we'll capture only metadata unless you opt-in for content retention.

[10:15] Elena Ruiz: what's success gating at the end of the 4 weeks?

[10:20] Dr. Maya Chen: success = hit >=92% precision on extraction, P95 latency <750ms for interactive flows on the chosen low-latency variant, and a clear path to production costs under our budget (TBD but target <$0.10 per processed doc average).

[10:40] Priya Nair: good. we'll design the bench to report those metrics plus a risk register: integration risks (VPC, SSO), model risks (hallucination), latency risks.

[10:55] Luis Ortega: technical deep-dive note — for latency we'll try LLAMA2-13B-int8 and Falcon-7B-int8 on our optimized kernels; for longer documents we may stream tokens and do chunked retrieval. small caveat: quantization can slightly change hallucination patterns — we'll monitor.

[11:25] Omar Rahman: any pitfalls from previous customers when doing domain-specific extraction?

[11:30] Priya Nair: common ones — mismatch in prompt engineering across teams, not enough annotated samples, and forgetting to include glossary/context during bench. also model compute choice affects how prompt length scales. we've seen teams assume big model = better and skip A/Bing smaller models first.

[11:50] Dr. Maya Chen: timeline recap?

[11:55] Sam Carter: recap: Sam to share model shortlist + cost spreadsheet by Friday (2026-07-03). Priya schedule a 2h bench planning session next Monday (2026-07-06). PolarisBio to deliver sanitized dataset + glossary by 2026-07-07. Redwood to run micro-bench and then full bench over next three weeks with deliverable report end of week 4. Security artefacts will be shared by Sam concurrently.

[12:35] Elena Ruiz: sounds good. also please include a sample benchmark spreadsheet that shows expected P95/P50 and cost columns.

[12:45] Sam Carter: will do. any blockers?

[12:52] Ayesha Khan: need the security one-pager and explicit KMS integration steps before we give network access.

[12:58] Sam Carter: understood, will prioritize.

[13:05] Dr. Maya Chen: thanks everyone — excited to see the bench.

[13:10] Sam Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the model shortlist sheet and schedule.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated; K-V cash -> K-V cache), filler words and overlap, and a few proper nouns corrected in the notes. Links referenced during call: model-shortlist-sheet (link shared in follow-up), security-onepager.pdf (to be sent), bench-template.xlsx (to be shared by Priya).
